rows.claim_text: Where a person holds French nationality as their sole nationality at the time of commencing employment in Norway, they are classified as an EU/EEA national for the purposes of free movement under EEA Agreement Art 28 and the Norwegian Immigration Act § 112.
rows.legal_basis: EEA Agreement Art 28; Norwegian Immigration Act § 112; Directive 2004/38/EC Art 2(1)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Foundational nationality-resolution claim; all downstream corridor claims depend on this classification being confirmed. Confirm that Norwegian domestic implementation of EEA Art 28 does not add conditions not present in EU law.

rows.claim_text: Where a person holds both French nationality and a non-EEA third-country nationality (dual national), the EEA-national classification in row 1 applies without qualification provided the French passport is the travel document used to enter Norway. The third-country nationality does not diminish EEA free-movement rights under Norwegian law.
rows.legal_basis: EEA Agreement Art 28; CJEU Case C-369/90 Micheletti; UDI Circular RS-2010-053
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Dual-nationality edge case — UDI circular reference requires Norwegian counsel verification. Check whether RS-2010-053 has been superseded by a later UDI directive.

rows.claim_text: French nationals who have acquired permanent residency in Norway prior to the current employment event are subject to the same rights and obligations as row 1 EEA nationals; the permanent residency status does not alter the applicable legislation determination for social security or tax.
rows.legal_basis: EEA Agreement Art 28; Directive 2004/38/EC Art 16; Norwegian Immigration Act § 115
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Pre-existing PR status edge case. Counsel to confirm that PR under § 115 does not create a separate applicable-legislation track under the Nordic Convention.

rows.claim_text: A French national commencing salaried employment in Norway (state of employment = NO) is subject to Norwegian social security legislation as the applicable legislation, pursuant to the general rule of lex loci laboris.
rows.legal_basis: Reg 883/2004 Art 11(3)(a); Nordic Convention on Social Security (2012) Art 6
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Core applicable-legislation claim. Norway is not EU but is EEA — confirm that Reg 883/2004 applies in Norway via EEA Agreement Annex VI and is not displaced by the Nordic Convention for FR→NO specifically.

rows.claim_text: Where the French national is posted to Norway by a French employer (posted worker, not locally hired), the applicable legislation remains French, not Norwegian, provided the posting does not exceed 24 months and the employer continues paying French social contributions.
rows.legal_basis: Reg 883/2004 Art 12(1); Nordic Convention on Social Security (2012) Art 7
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Posted-worker carve-out. This is an INFO disposition — counsel must confirm the engine is correct that merely explaining the 24-month posted-worker rule does not constitute advice requiring ROUTE classification.

rows.claim_text: Where a French national simultaneously pursues self-employment in France and salaried employment in Norway, the applicable legislation for social security is determined on a substantial activity assessment, not automatically lex loci laboris; the engine routes this scenario to ROUTE disposition.
rows.legal_basis: Reg 883/2004 Art 13(3); Administrative Commission Decision A1 (2010)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Multi-state worker scenario. Already classified ROUTE by engine. Counsel to confirm ROUTE is the correct disposition and that the substantial-activity test description in claim_text is legally accurate without itself constituting advice.

rows.claim_text: The UK-exit protocol and any transitional provisions under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement do not apply to the FR→NO corridor. Reg 883/2004 (as incorporated into the EEA Agreement) is the operative coordination instrument for FR→NO regardless of post-Brexit rule changes affecting UK corridors.
rows.legal_basis: EEA Agreement Annex VI; Reg 883/2004; EU-UK TCA (inapplicable — explicitly excluded)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. Brexit-exclusion claim — ensures engine does not incorrectly apply UK-exit transitional rules to FR→NO cases. Counsel to confirm this exclusion is unambiguous and that no EEA-specific Brexit spillover provisions exist.

rows.claim_text: When a user's case facts indicate simultaneous multi-state employment, cross-border self-employment, or a posting exceeding 24 months, the engine MUST NOT surface a determination of applicable legislation to the user. The engine MUST instead display a routing prompt directing the user to seek advice from a regulated professional. Surfacing any applicable-legislation determination in these scenarios would constitute regulated legal advice under French and Norwegian professional rules.
rows.legal_basis: French law 71-1130 Art 54 (consultation juridique); Norwegian Domstolloven § 218; Reg 883/2004 Art 13 (trigger condition)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for France counsel call. This is the critical advice-routing gate claim for the FR→NO corridor. Counsel must confirm (a) that the described routing behaviour keeps the engine on the INFO side of the regulated-advice line under both French and Norwegian professional rules, and (b) that the routing prompt wording (to be provided separately) is adequate. This is the highest-priority claim for the France counsel call.

rows.claim_text: Where a person holds Spanish nationality as their sole nationality at the time of commencing employment in Ireland, they are a Union citizen entitled to free movement of workers into Ireland and require no employment permit or prior immigration permission; Ireland must admit and permit them to take up employment on the same basis as an Irish national.
rows.legal_basis: TFEU Art 45; Directive 2004/38/EC Art 2(1); European Communities (Free Movement of Persons) Regulations 2015 (S.I. No. 548 of 2015) (Ireland)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for Irish counsel review. Foundational nationality-resolution claim; all downstream ES→IE claims depend on this classification being confirmed. Counsel to confirm Ireland's domestic implementation (S.I. 548/2015) of Directive 2004/38/EC adds no conditions not present in EU law, and that Ireland's non-Schengen status does not create an additional entry formality for an EU worker.

rows.claim_text: Where a person is a non-EU third-country national who is merely resident in Spain (e.g. holds a Spanish residence/work authorisation but not Spanish nationality), that Spanish residence does NOT confer any derived right of free movement to Ireland. Such a person requires an Irish employment permit AND separate Irish immigration permission before commencing employment in Ireland; the move must be treated as a third-country immigration case, not an intra-EU transfer.
rows.legal_basis: Directive 2004/38/EC Art 3(1) (scope limited to Union citizens and qualifying family members); Employment Permits Act 2006 as amended by Employment Permits (Amendment) Act 2014 (Ireland); Immigration Act 2004 (Ireland) s.4
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for Irish counsel review. Critical distinguishing claim for the ES→IE corridor: a common misconception is that Spanish residence transfers free-movement rights. Counsel to confirm (i) that no derived free-movement right arises from residence alone, (ii) the correct Irish employment-permit route (e.g. Critical Skills vs General), and (iii) that Ireland's non-participation in Schengen means a separate Irish immigration permission is required irrespective of any Spanish residence card.

rows.claim_text: Where a person holds Spanish nationality together with a non-EU third-country nationality (dual national), the Union-citizen classification in row 1 applies without qualification, provided the Spanish (EU) passport is the travel document relied upon for entry and employment in Ireland. The third-country nationality does not diminish free-movement rights and does not trigger the employment-permit requirement of row 2.
rows.legal_basis: CJEU Case C-369/90 Micheletti; Directive 2004/38/EC Art 2(1)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for Irish counsel review. Dual-nationality edge case. Counsel to confirm Micheletti (a Member State may not restrict the effects of the grant of the nationality of another Member State) is correctly applied and that Irish practice recognises the Spanish nationality for free-movement purposes regardless of the concurrent third-country nationality.

rows.claim_text: A Spanish national commencing salaried employment in Ireland (state of employment = IE) is subject to Irish social security legislation (PRSI) as the applicable legislation, pursuant to the general rule of lex loci laboris.
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. Core applicable-legislation claim for ES→IE. Both states are EU Members so Reg 883/2004 applies directly. Counsel to confirm no bilateral instrument displaces the lex loci laboris rule for this pairing.

rows.claim_text: Where the Spanish national is posted to Ireland by a Spanish employer (posted worker, not locally hired), the applicable legislation remains Spanish, not Irish, provided the anticipated duration of the posting does not exceed 24 months and the person is not sent to replace another posted worker; the employer should obtain a Portable Document A1 from the Spanish institution.
rows.legal_basis: Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 12(1); Reg (EC) 987/2009 Art 15 (A1 issuance procedure)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. Posted-worker carve-out. This is an INFO disposition — counsel must confirm the engine is correct that stating the 24-month posted-worker rule and the A1 requirement does not itself constitute advice requiring ROUTE classification.

rows.claim_text: Where the Spanish national normally pursues activity in two or more Member States (e.g. simultaneous employment in Spain and Ireland, or cross-border self-employment), the applicable legislation is NOT determined automatically by lex loci laboris but by a substantial-activity / registered-office assessment under the multi-state rules; the engine classifies this scenario as ROUTE and does not surface a determination.
rows.legal_basis: Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 13(1)-(3); Reg (EC) 987/2009 Art 16; Administrative Commission Decision A1 (2010)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. Multi-state worker scenario, already classified ROUTE by the engine. Counsel to confirm ROUTE is the correct disposition and that the substantial-activity test description is legally accurate without itself constituting advice.

rows.claim_text: When a user's case facts indicate simultaneous multi-state employment, cross-border self-employment, or a posting expected to exceed 24 months, the engine MUST NOT surface a determination of applicable legislation to the user. It MUST instead display a routing prompt directing the user to a regulated professional (an Irish solicitor and/or a Spanish abogado), because rendering an individualised determination on these facts would cross into reserved/regulated legal advice.
rows.legal_basis: Legal Services Regulation Act 2015 (Ireland); Solicitors Acts 1954–2015 (Ireland); Ley 34/2006 de acceso a las profesiones de Abogado y Procurador de los Tribunales (Spain); Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 13 (trigger condition)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. This is the critical advice-routing gate claim for the ES→IE corridor. Counsel must confirm (a) that the described routing behaviour keeps the engine on the INFO side of the regulated-advice line under both Irish (LSRA 2015 / Solicitors Acts) and Spanish rules, and (b) that the trigger conditions (multi-state / posting>24m / cross-border self-employment) are the right set.

rows.claim_text: Where a person holds Norwegian nationality as their sole nationality at the time of relocating to France, they are an EEA national entitled to free movement into France; they may enter, reside and take up employment in France without a visa or work permit, subject only to declaratory registration formalities.
rows.legal_basis: EEA Agreement Art 28; Directive 2004/38/EC Art 2(1) (incorporated into the EEA Agreement by EEA Joint Committee Decision No 158/2007); Code de l'entrée et du séjour des étrangers et du droit d'asile (CESEDA) Art L233-1
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for French counsel review. Foundational nationality-resolution claim; all downstream NO→FR claims depend on this EEA classification being confirmed. Counsel to confirm that French implementation (CESEDA L233-1 et seq.) treats Norwegian EEA nationals on the same footing as EU nationals and adds no conditions absent from EU/EEA law.

rows.claim_text: Where a person holds both French nationality and Norwegian nationality (dual national), the person is a French national on French territory and a Union citizen; no EEA free-movement formality or residence permit is required. The Norwegian nationality does not subordinate or qualify the French nationality for the purposes of entry, residence, or employment in France.
rows.legal_basis: TFEU Art 20; CJEU Case C-369/90 Micheletti; EEA Agreement Art 28
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for French counsel review. Dual FR/NO national edge case (directly relevant to the repatriation profile). Counsel to confirm that a returning dual national is treated purely as a French national for immigration purposes and that Micheletti prevents any diminution of that status.

rows.claim_text: A Norwegian national who held a prior French residence status before the current move (e.g. a returning former resident) is subject to the same rights and obligations as a row 1 EEA national; any pre-existing or lapsed residence status does not alter the applicable-legislation determination for social security or tax, which is decided afresh on the current employment facts.
rows.legal_basis: EEA Agreement Art 28; Directive 2004/38/EC Art 16; CESEDA Art L233-2
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for French counsel review. Pre-existing residence-status edge case. Counsel to confirm that lapsed/prior French residence does not create a separate applicable-legislation track and that permanent-residence acquisition under Directive 2004/38/EC Art 16 is correctly reflected in French practice.

rows.claim_text: A Norwegian national who becomes locally employed in France (state of employment = FR, no retained Norwegian employer) is subject to French social security legislation as the applicable legislation under lex loci laboris. Reg (EC) 883/2004 applies to Norway as an EEA State via the EEA Agreement, notwithstanding that Norway is EEA and not EU.
rows.legal_basis: Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 11(3)(a); EEA Agreement Annex VI (Social Security)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. Core applicable-legislation claim for locally-hired NO→FR. The Norway-is-EEA-not-EU point is the non-obvious flag — counsel to confirm Reg 883/2004 applies in Norway via EEA Annex VI and is the operative coordination instrument for NO→FR.

rows.claim_text: Where the Norwegian national RETAINS their Norwegian employer and is posted to work in France (posted worker, not locally hired), the applicable legislation remains Norwegian, not French, provided the anticipated posting does not exceed 24 months, the person is not replacing another posted worker, and the direct employment relationship with the Norwegian employer is maintained; a Portable Document A1 should be obtained from the Norwegian institution (NAV).
rows.legal_basis: Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 12(1); Reg (EC) 987/2009 Art 15 (A1 procedure); EEA Agreement Annex VI
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. This is the defining employer-retention scenario for the NO→FR corridor. INFO disposition — counsel must confirm that explaining the 24-month posting rule, the A1 requirement, and the retained-employer condition does not itself constitute advice requiring ROUTE, and must confirm the exit-side Norwegian employer obligations that survive the move.

rows.claim_text: Where the Norwegian national transitions to French social security, periods of insurance, employment or residence completed under Norwegian legislation are aggregated (totalised) with French periods for the acquisition, retention or calculation of benefits; facts and events occurring in Norway are given equal treatment.
rows.legal_basis: Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 6 (aggregation of periods); Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 5 (equal treatment of benefits, income, facts or events); EEA Agreement Annex VI
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. Totalization claim. Counsel to confirm that stating the aggregation principle (Art 6) and equal-treatment principle (Art 5) is an INFO information point and that any individualised calculation of a specific benefit entitlement would need to ROUTE.

rows.claim_text: Where the Norwegian national normally pursues activity in two or more States (e.g. continues substantial Norwegian activity while also working in France, or cross-border self-employment), the applicable legislation is NOT determined automatically by lex loci laboris but by a substantial-activity / registered-office assessment under the multi-state rules; the engine classifies this scenario as ROUTE and does not surface a determination.
rows.legal_basis: Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 13(1)-(3); Reg (EC) 987/2009 Art 16; Administrative Commission Decision A1 (2010)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. Multi-state worker scenario, already classified ROUTE by the engine. Especially live for NO→FR because the retained-employer profile can shade into multi-state activity. Counsel to confirm ROUTE is correct and the substantial-activity description is accurate without constituting advice.

rows.claim_text: When a user's case facts indicate simultaneous multi-state employment, cross-border self-employment, or a posting expected to exceed 24 months, the engine MUST NOT surface a determination of applicable legislation to the user. It MUST instead display a routing prompt directing the user to a regulated professional (a French avocat and, for exit-side employer obligations, appropriate Norwegian counsel), because rendering an individualised determination on these facts would cross into consultation juridique / rettslig bistand.
rows.legal_basis: French Loi n°71-1130 du 31 décembre 1971 Art 54 (consultation juridique); Norwegian domstolloven (exit-side legal-service provider duties — exact provision TBC by NO counsel); Reg (EC) 883/2004 Art 13 (trigger condition)
rows.notes: CLAIM STUB — UNATTESTED. Queued for counsel review. This is the critical advice-routing gate claim for the NO→FR corridor. Counsel must confirm (a) that the routing behaviour keeps the engine on the INFO side of the regulated-advice line under French rules (Loi 71-1130 Art 54) and Norwegian exit-side rules (domstolloven — exact provision to be confirmed), and (b) that the retained-employer / employer-retention angle does not introduce an additional trigger the engine must route.
